title: Getting a Ticket for Machu Picchu Is Now a Little Easier
paragraphs: Machu Picchu, the 15th-century Inca citadel high in the Andes mountains of Peru, is one of the most popular tourist attractions in South America. However, because the number of daily visitors is strictly limited, getting a ticket can be difficult, especially during the busiest months. Now, Peru's government has introduced changes that may make the process a little easier.

In September 2026, Peru's Ministry of Culture began testing a new system for selling tickets on its official website, Tu Boleto. Previously, buyers could reserve tickets for three hours before paying for them. According to reports, this allowed a small number of travel agencies to hold large numbers of tickets, and when reservations were not completed, the tickets were not available to other visitors in the meantime.

Under the new system, which started as a 30-day trial on September 22, this advance reservation step has been eliminated. Instead, buyers choose a date, a route and a time slot, and they have 15 minutes to complete their payment. If they do not pay in time, the ticket is immediately released for other buyers. Once the payment is confirmed, the ticket is issued in the visitor's name and linked to their identification. According to the Ministry of Culture, the aim is to make sure that the availability shown on the website matches the tickets that visitors can actually buy. During the trial, officials will also decide whether the 15-minute payment window should be kept, extended or shortened.

However, the new system does not change the number of visitors allowed each day. Machu Picchu can receive up to 5,600 visitors a day in the high season and 4,500 a day during the rest of the year. Some tickets are also sold in person in the nearby town of Machu Picchu Pueblo, but these can sell out quickly.
Visitors are therefore still advised to plan carefully and to buy their tickets only from official sources.
